advances.name: The Surveyor's Chain
advances.description: Sighting frames and measured chains turn a track into a route with a known length. A governor who can say how far away a thing is can also say when he will hear about it.

advances.name: Bound Mortar
advances.description: Ash, lime and rubble set into a stone that pours. Walls no longer wait on a quarry, and a builder's estimate finally means something.

advances.name: The Written Census
advances.description: Households counted, land measured, obligations written down. Being legible to the state is the beginning of being governed by it — and the end of a clerk's quiet arithmetic.

advances.name: The Fallow Year
advances.description: Land rested and land planted in turn, and a bean crop where the grain stood last. Yields that no longer fall away after a decade of the same furrow.

advances.name: The Assembled Library
advances.description: Copyists paid by the roll, and a catalogue that says where each is kept. What one generation worked out, the next no longer has to.

advances.name: The Measured Fall
advances.description: A channel that drops a hand's breadth in a mile and runs for forty. Water arrives clean at the height it is needed, and the city stops drinking from the river it fouls.

advances.name: The Marching Camp
advances.description: Every soldier a labourer, every halt a fortified square dug to the same plan. Men who build a camp nightly can raise anything else in half the time.

advances.name: The Posted Law
advances.description: Statutes cut in bronze and set up where anyone may read them. A rule a magistrate cannot quietly reinterpret is worth more to the ruled than a generous one he can.

advances.name: Harbour Works
advances.description: Moles thrown out into deep water and a basin that silts slowly. Ships that can be worked in any weather change what a season is worth.

advances.name: The Standing Archive
advances.description: Records kept past the death of the man who made them, in a building with a roof and a budget. The difference between a people who know a thing and a people who once knew it.

advances.name: The Public Bath
advances.description: Hypocausts, hot rooms and cold plunges, open to anyone with a small coin. A daily proof that the state spends something on people who will never be asked to a banquet.

advances.name: The Corn Dole
advances.description: A measured ration against the bad year, distributed by ticket and by name. It is not charity and it is not bribery: it is the state admitting it owes something in return.

advances.name: Provincial Administration
advances.description: Salaried officials with defined terms, audited accounts, and a road for the report to travel. An empire finally able to see its own edges.
